skill.name: requesting-code-review
skill.description: Requests a structured code review after implementation work, using git ranges and a code-reviewer template to assess readiness.
skill.summary: Request structured code reviews before merge or continued implementation.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, placeholder labels, and bounded local git commands. Manual review of SKILL.zip found only a duplicate SKILL.md file. One medium semantic issue remains because the git diff template does not require validation of range placeholders before shell execution.

remediation.issue: Git diff template accepts unvalidated range placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Require BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA to be verified as commit hashes or trusted refs before using them in shell commands.

remediation.issue: A redundant SKILL.zip archive forces manual marketplace review.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the archive from the skill package or document why it is required.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Git Range Placeholders
semantic_findings.description: The review template shows git diff commands with BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA placeholders but does not require validation before shell execution. If copied from untrusted text, those placeholders could become command injection input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are legitimate git review commands, but the template inserts placeholder values into shell examples without validation guidance. The risk depends on who supplies the range values.

content.value_statement: Code changes need focused review before they reach main. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured review workflow with git range context and severity-based feedback.
actual_capabilities: Guides users to collect base and head git references for a review range.
Dispatches a code-reviewer subagent with implementation details and requirements context.
Uses a checklist covering code quality, architecture, testing, requirements, and production readiness.
Organizes review feedback into Critical, Important, and Minor severity groups.
Requests a clear merge readiness assessment with concise technical reasoning.
Encourages fixing critical and important issues before continuing development.
limitations: Requires a compatible code-reviewer subagent and Task tool workflow.
Depends on accurate base and head git references from the user or agent.
Does not guarantee tests are executed unless the surrounding workflow runs them.
Reviews are only as complete as the provided requirements and diff context.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge review
use_cases.description: Check a feature branch before merging to main and identify blocking issues early.

use_cases.title: Plan milestone review
use_cases.description: Review completed tasks against a written plan before moving to the next batch.

use_cases.title: Subagent workflow checkpoint
use_cases.description: Add structured review gates to AI-assisted development so issues do not compound.

prompt_templates.title: Review my last change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner checkpoint after a small task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use requesting-code-review to review my last completed change against the task request. Highlight critical, important, and minor issues.

prompt_templates.title: Review a completed feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the feature I just implemented against the acceptance criteria. Include strengths, issues, recommendations, and merge readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Review a plan milestone
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after several planned tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use requesting-code-review for the completed plan milestone. Compare the diff with the plan and identify gaps before I continue.

prompt_templates.title: Review a release range
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release readiness review with explicit git range.
prompt_templates.prompt: Request a code review for this release range. Verify architecture, testing evidence, requirement coverage, regressions, and production readiness.

output_examples.input: I finished a bug fix and want a quick review before continuing.
output: The skill collects the intended review range and implementation summary.
It asks the reviewer to compare the change against the bug fix requirements.
The result lists strengths, severity-ranked issues, recommendations, and readiness.

output_examples.input: I completed three tasks from a deployment plan.
output: The skill sends the completed milestone and plan context to the reviewer.
The reviewer checks code quality, architecture, testing, requirements, and release concerns.
The final assessment states whether to proceed, merge, or fix issues first.

output_examples.input: I need an independent review before merging a feature branch.
output: The workflow frames the review around the branch diff and expected behavior.
Critical and important issues are separated from minor cleanup items.
The response gives a clear merge decision with technical reasoning.

best_practices: Provide the implementation summary and requirements with every review request.
Use exact base and head commits so the reviewer examines the intended diff.
Fix critical and important issues before proceeding to the next task.
anti_patterns: Requesting review with no requirements, plan, or acceptance criteria.
Ignoring clear findings because the change appears small.
Treating minor cleanup feedback as a release blocker without technical cause.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews code changes against implementation details, requirements, and git range context.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured AI review checkpoint before human review or merge decisions.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks the reviewer to check testing evidence, but separate test commands may still be needed.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after major tasks, before merging, or when a fresh technical review would reduce risk.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect strengths, issues by severity, recommendations, and a clear readiness assessment.
